messages.text: Anyone else seeing DocVault uploads crawling this morning? Trying to attach a signed wire authorization and it's been spinning for over 2 min. Normally instant.
Yep, same here. Uploaded a PDF under 1MB and it took about 90 seconds. Downloads seem fine though, just uploads.
Looking now. Seeing elevated p95 on the DocVault upload endpoint, about 40s vs a normal 1-2s. Treating this as SEV3 for now, will bump if it spreads. Opening a ticket, INC-4417.
Impact on our side: wire release packages are stalling because we can't attach the supporting docs. We have a few time-sensitive ones queued for the noon cutoff.
Understood. Workaround for now: hold the docs locally and attach once uploads recover, or have the approver sign off on the wire console with a note referencing INC-4417. I'll ping when it's safe.
Heads up from Risk: our onboarding doc review queue is backing up too. Is this DocVault only, or is anything upstream like AuthSSO involved?
AuthSSO looks clean, token validation is normal. Narrowing it to the DocVault storage write path. Thread pool is saturated and there's a big backlog of writes.

Might be me. A DataLake backfill job kicked off at 7:30 and it's bulk-copying archived records into DocVault storage for the analytics team. It's hammering the same write path. I should've scheduled it off-hours.
That lines up with the saturation start time. Michael, can you pause the backfill? Don't kill it, just suspend so it can resume from the checkpoint.
Paused. Checkpoint saved. I'll rerun it tonight with throttling at 10 concurrent writers and add a note to the job runbook. CreditScoring's nightly pull is unaffected as far as I can tell.
Update: write queue drained, upload p95 back to about 1.5s. Resolved, downgrading INC-4417 to monitoring. Wire room and Risk, please retry your uploads and shout if anything still hangs.
Confirmed, uploads are instant again and the queued wire packages are attached. Thanks all.
